successors.note: 'The Eastern Khanate ended in 1211' (the prince 'was killed in Kashgar by the rebels in 1211'). The same page has the rebels in Kashgar surrender to Kuchlug, 'who had usurped the Kara-Khitai throne', in 1214; it does not say who ruled the Tarim cities in 1212-1213, and the Kuchlug page is silent on Kashgar's date. The land therefore passes to the Qara Khitai realm under Kuchlug, in 1214 for Kashgar (kara-khitans /ledger gain of 1214), with 1212-1213 held by the Kashgar rebels. Confidence 2.

capitals.name: Balasagun (Burana)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Balasagun (942-1130)'; 'The Eastern Khanate had its capital at Balasaghun and later Kashgar.' The Qara Khitai took Balasagun in 1134.

capitals.name: Kashgar
capitals.note: Infobox 'Kashgar (1130-1211)'; the Qara Khitai attacked it in the summer of 1131 (Yelü Dashi page). Coordinates from the gazetteer.

rulers.name: Ebu Shuca Sulayman
rulers.note: Eastern ruler list of the Kara-Khanid page (the extracted table was flagged as garbled): 'Ebu Shuca Sulayman 1042-1056'. He reigned from 1042 in the undivided khanate (the split is 'in the 1040s'); this dossier starts in 1046, Cliopatria's first Eastern shape, so he is listed from 1046.

rulers.name: Muhammad bin Yusuph
rulers.note: Eastern ruler list of the Kara-Khanid page, re-read for the review fix: 'Muhammad bin Yusuph 1056-1057'. The page does not say which city he ruled from.

rulers.name: Umar

rulers.note: Ruler list 1128-1158. The Yelü Dashi page has Dashi deposing 'Ibrahim II' in 1134, which does not fit a reign to 1158 for the Eastern khan.

rulers.name: Ebul Feth Muhammad

keyframe_review.note: 1046-1055, 984,464 km2: Zhetysu with Balasagun, the Fergana valley, the Tarim from Kashgar to Khotan (Khotan conquered 1006) and the Pamir edge. Matches the page's 'Balasagun (then the capital of the Karakhanid state) in Zhetysu, Kashgar in Xinjiang, Uzgen in Fergana' and 'When the two states were formed, Fergana fell into realm of the Eastern Khanate'. The page gives no area, so the infobox comparison is not possible.
1056-1065, 981,541 km2: 36 cells (9,100 km2) drop out and 26 (6,600 km2) are added on the Pamir-Alay edge (70.6-77.3 E, 35.8-40.3 N); unverified: page silent on this step.

1066-1071, 917,178 km2: the Fergana valley (218 cells, 55,000 km2) passes to Cliopatria's Western row. The year is Cliopatria's and unverified, but the transfer itself is on the pages: Fergana was the Eastern Khanate's at the split, 'frequently contested' afterwards, and 'was later captured by Ibrahim and became part of the Western Khanate' (Kara-Khanid page; Ibrahim Tamghach Khan, Western khan to 1068); the Ibrahim page has him force 'the Karakhanid rulers of Farghana to acknowledge him as their suzerain' in 1059/60, six years before this shape. The Malik-Shah I page still has the Eastern ruler Hasan at Uzkand (Uzgen) in 1087 and the Yelü Dashi page has the Western Karakhanids defeated at Khujand in 1137 with Fergana consolidated by Dashi, so the Western hold was not lasting. Kept as drawn (years from Cliopatria); see the Western dossier.
1072-1084: same cells as 1066 (years only); no page dates a change.

1085-1093: same cells as 1066 (43 km2 of rounding). The Malik-Shah I page has the Seljuks take Kara-Khanid castles in 1087 'especially Bukhara, Samarkand, Balasagun, Isfijab and Kashgar' and the Eastern ruler Hasan ibn Suleiman submit at Uzkand as a vassal; the Kara-Khanid page says the Eastern Khanate 'was a Seljuk vassal for only a short time'. A vassal status with no loss of land: the shape stands.

Aksu and Tumshuk are inside the Cliopatria shape already (Aksu from 1046); Kucha (Kuqa, 39 cells) is not, and Cliopatria's Qocho shape keeps it to 1125. The page says 'by 1096', so the Kucha addition is dated to 1096 in the ledger.

Years only: this shape (with Kucha, 3,109 cells) holds 1126-1133; the new keyframe _1134 carries the Tarim rump (1,249 cells) to 1211, and the ledger loss of 1134 takes the 1,860 other cells (Zhetysu, the Tian Shan, the Alay and the Pamir edge). Infobox area not available.

correction.text: the Tarim Basin part of the Eastern shape: Kashgar, Yarkand, Khotan, Aksu and Kucha, the 'Kashgar (1130-1211)' of the infobox

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1134-1211: the Tarim rump at Kashgar, a Qara Khitai vassal (infobox 'Qara Khitai vassal (1141-1212)'; 'Despite losing to the Qara Khitai, the Karakhanid dynasty remained in power as their vassals'). Zhetysu is lost with Balasagun in 1134 (Qara Khitai page) and the Qara Khitai 'went on to conquer Kashgar, Khotan, and Beshbalik' after 1137, but the Kashgar khans are still there to put down rebellions in 1204 and to be killed in 1211. Cliopatria hands the whole Eastern shape to its Kara-Khitans row in 1139; the tint should be a vassal's. Extent of the rump is the reading of the Kashgar capital and the 1204 rebellions at Kashgar and Khotan (confidence 2). Review fix: the Qara Khitai overlordship of the rump is now in the ledger (vassal_start 1141, vassal_end 1211). After the killing of 1211 the Kara-Khanid page has the Kashgar rebels surrender to Kuchlug in 1214 (it is silent on the other Tarim cities in 1212-1213); the kara-khitans dossier draws the rump as direct land from 1214.

region.text: the Eastern Khanate, 'capital at Balasaghun and later Kashgar'

ledger.note: 1046: the Eastern Khanate of the Kara-Khanids is formed at Balasagun. 'The Khanate split into the Eastern and Western Khanates in the 1040s.' The page gives the decade; 1046 is Cliopatria's first year for the two rows.

1066: the Fergana valley passes to the Western Khanate. Cliopatria's step; the Kara-Khanid page is silent on the date ('When the two states were formed, Fergana fell into realm of the Eastern Khanate'; the border was 'frequently contested'). The page goes on: Fergana 'was later captured by Ibrahim and became part of the Western Khanate' (Ibrahim Tamghach Khan, Western khan to 1068), so the transfer is on the page and falls before 1068; only the year 1066 is Cliopatria's (reviewer ia-01-g). The Ibrahim Tamghach Khan page (second page, not in the dossier's first budget) has Ibrahim 'force the Karakhanid rulers of Farghana to acknowledge him as their suzerain' in 1059/60, which puts the transfer, or the suzerainty that preceded it, about six years before Cliopatria's 1066; the Western dossier's mirror gain carries the same Cliopatria year.

region.text: Balasagun, Isfijab and Kashgar, the Eastern lands to which the Seljuk campaign reached

ledger.note: 1087: Malik-Shah's Seljuks invade the Karakhanid lands as far as the Eastern Khanate. 'In 1087 ... Malik-Shah decided to organize another expedition to Transoxiana', took Kara-Khanid castles 'especially Bukhara, Samarkand, Balasagun, Isfijab and Kashgar', and at Uzkand 'the Eastern Kara-Khanid ruler Hasan ibn Suleiman' submitted as a vassal. The Kara-Khanid page has the Seljuk campaign reach 'Talas and Zhetysu' and Kashgar submit.

1089: the Eastern khan is a Seljuk vassal and the campaign is over. 'the entire Turkistan Region, up to the borders of China, was brought under Seljuk rule in 1089'; the Kara-Khanid page: 'the Eastern Khanate was a Seljuk vassal for only a short time'. The Seljuk dossier should carry the vassal_start; the end of the vassalage is not dated by either page.

1089: the Eastern Khanate is a Seljuk vassal. Malik-Shah I page: 'the Eastern Kara-Khanid ruler Hasan ibn Suleiman came to Malik-Shah and agreed to be his vassal and pay taxes' (in the 1087 paragraph, with no year of its own) and 'the entire Turkistan Region, up to the borders of China ... was brought under Seljuk rule in 1089'; the Kara-Khanid page: 'the Eastern Khanate was a Seljuk vassal for only a short time' (no years; its infobox runs 'Seljuk vassal (1089-1141)' for the Khanate as a whole). The year is the page's, the region is the contest zone (reading). Added after the review (ia-01-g).

1092: a bridging year. The pages give no end for the short Seljuk vassalage of the Eastern Khanate. Malik-Shah died on 19 November 1092 ('Malik-Shah died on 19 November 1092 while he was hunting') and 'the Seljuk Empire fell into chaos'; the page does not say what the Kara-Khanids did then. Confidence 1.

1096: Kucha, Aksu and Tumshuk are in Kara-Khanid hands. The Qocho page: 'By 1096, Qocho had lost Aksu, Tumshuk, and Kucha to the Kara-Khanid Khanate'; the year is a latest date, not the year of the conquest.
1130: the Eastern capital moves from Balasagun to Kashgar. The infobox: 'Balasagun (942-1130); Kashgar (1130-1211)'.

region.text: Balasagun, Zhetysu and the Tian Shan: the whole non-Tarim part of the Eastern 1126 shape (Kucha added), 1,860 cells

ledger.note: 1134: Yelü Dashi takes Balasagun and the Chu valley. 'In 1134 he conquered the Karakhanid city of Balasaghun'; the Kara-Khanid page: 'Yelü occupied Balasagun on the Chu River'. The page names the city; the extent is the reading (confidence 2): all of the Eastern 1126 shape (Kucha added) that is not the Tarim rump, 1,860 cells or about 470,000 km2 (Zhetysu 1,306 cells, and 554 cells, about 140,000 km2, of the Tian Shan interior, the Alay and the Pamir edge). The first version named only Zhetysu and left the 554 cells leaving the shape with no event (reviewer ia-01-g). The Tarim rump stays with the Khanate, as keyframe _1134 has it. Mirrored in the kara-khitans gain of 1134.

region.text: the Tarim Basin part of the Eastern shape: Kashgar, Yarkand, Khotan, Aksu and Kucha, the 'Kashgar (1130-1211)' of the infobox

ledger.note: 1141: the Eastern Khanate, left at Kashgar, becomes a Qara Khitai vassal. Kara-Khanid infobox: 'Qara Khitai vassal (1141-1212)'; the page: 'Despite losing to the Qara Khitai, the Karakhanid dynasty remained in power as their vassals'. 1141 is the year of the Battle of Qatwan (kara-khitans dossier). The land is the Tarim rump of keyframe _1134; the kara-khitans dossier carries the mirror (/ledger vassal_start 1141) with this dossier as the vassal.

1204: the Qara Khitai put down a rebellion at Kashgar. 'In 1204, a rebellion of the Eastern Kara-Khanid in Kashgar was suppressed by the Kara-Khitai'; the Qara Khitai page adds Khotan: the Qara Khitai 'put down a rebellion in Khotan and Kashgar'.
1204: the Kashgar rebellion is suppressed and the Qara Khitai overlordship stands.

region.text: the Tarim Basin part of the Eastern shape: Kashgar, Yarkand, Khotan, Aksu and Kucha, the 'Kashgar (1130-1211)' of the infobox

ledger.note: 1211: the vassalage ends when the Eastern prince is killed at Kashgar by the rebels. 'The Eastern Khanate ended in 1211'; he 'was killed in Kashgar by the rebels in 1211' (the infobox runs the Qara Khitai vassalage of the Khanate as a whole to 1212). Kuchlug usurps the Qara Khitai throne in the same year (Kuchlug page) and the Kashgar rebels surrender to him in 1214.

region.text: the Tarim Basin part of the Eastern shape: Kashgar, Yarkand, Khotan, Aksu and Kucha, the 'Kashgar (1130-1211)' of the infobox

ledger.note: 1211: the Eastern Khanate ends. 'The Eastern Khanate ended in 1211'; the prince 'was killed in Kashgar by the rebels in 1211'. The Kara-Khanid page has the Kashgar rebels surrender to Kuchlug in 1214, so the Tarim rump is held by the rebels in 1212-1213 and passes to the Qara Khitai under Kuchlug in 1214; it does not say who ruled the other Tarim cities in 1212-1213.

wars.name: Seljuk campaign into Talas and Zhetysu
wars.outcome: Seljuk victory: the Eastern khan Hasan ibn Suleiman submits at Uzkand and the Karakhanids of Kashgar 'declared their submission'; the vassalage lasts 'only a short time'.
wars.note: The Kara-Khanid page gives the campaign without a year; Malik-Shah I dates the expedition to 1087 and the submission of Turkestan to 1089.

wars.name: Qara Khitai conquest of the Eastern Khanate
wars.outcome: Dashi is repelled at Kashgar in the summer of 1131, takes Balasagun in 1134 and, 'after 1137', Kashgar, Khotan and Beshbalik; the Karakhanid dynasty stays in power at Kashgar as Qara Khitai vassals from 1141.
wars.note: The Qara Khitai page dates the attack on Kashgar to 1131 and the conquests after 1137 without years; the Kara-Khanid infobox gives the vassalage as 1141-1212.

wars.name: Kashgar rebellion against the Qara Khitai
wars.outcome: The rebellion of 1204 is suppressed; the last Eastern prince is released and killed at Kashgar by rebels in 1211, ending the khanate.

certainty.note: Steppe, mountain and oasis frontiers throughout, no survey or treaty line; the Fergana-Zhetysu border with the Western Khanate was 'frequently contested'.

notes:
One state or three: Wikidata Q494354 is shared by Cliopatria's Kara-Khanids (850-1045), Eastern Kara-Khanids (1046-1138) and Western Karakhanid Khanate (1046-1084). The page lists one khanate that 'split into the Eastern and Western Khanates in the 1040s'; the two halves have different capitals (Balasagun and then Kashgar, against Samarkand) and different fates (the East ends in 1211 at Kashgar, the West in 1212 at Samarkand), so they are written as two states; the unified Khanate is the dossier kara-khanids (840-1045).
End moved: Cliopatria's row stops in 1138 and hands its whole shape to Kara-Khitans in 1139; the pages keep the Eastern khans at Kashgar as Qara Khitai vassals until 1211, so the new keyframe _1134 holds the Tarim rump to 1211. The kara-khitans dossier carries the vassal_start (1141) and vassal_end (1211) for counterpart eastern-kara-khanids. The Seljuk campaign of 1087-1089 is a contest here, followed (review fix) by a short Seljuk vassalage 1089-1092 (the end is a bridging year, confidence 1); great-seljuk-empire should carry the mirror pair. The Qara Khitai overlordship 1141-1211 is now a vassal_start/vassal_end pair here as well as in kara-khitans.
Unsettled: (1) the Fergana valley (Cliopatria gives it to the West in 1066; the pages say the East held it at the split, the East's ruler is at Uzkand in 1087, and the West loses it to Dashi in 1137); (2) the extent of the rump after 1134: the page names Kashgar and Khotan, not a boundary; (3) the ruler list is from a garbled table (Ibrahim bin Ahmad 1128-1158 against the Yelü Dashi page's Ibrahim II deposed in 1134; Yusuf's start year '?'); (4) 'After 1137 ... conquer Kashgar, Khotan, and Beshbalik' (Qara Khitai page) against the Karakhanids staying on at Kashgar to 1211. No page gives an area, so the infobox comparison was impossible. Qocho page's Kucha, Aksu and Tumshuk (by 1096) matched by the qocho-kingdom dossier's loss event. Pages: Kara-Khanid Khanate (three queries), Malik-Shah I, Qara Khitai, Yelü Dashi, Qocho: five distinct pages.
Missing: the Eastern Khanate's invasion of Transoxiana and brief occupation of Termez 'at the beginning of the 12th century' (Kara-Khanid page, undated); the Khitan frontier of the 11th century; Uzgen as a seat.
Review fixes (ia-01-g, 2026-10-19): (1) the 1134 loss now names the whole non-Tarim part of the Eastern shape (1,860 cells), not only Zhetysu (1,306), and kara-khitans gains the same cells; (2) vassal pairs added for the Qara Khitai (1141-1211) and the Seljuks (1089-1092); (3) the ruler list now starts Sulayman at 1046 and has the reigns of 1056-1059 and Umar (1075), from the page's list; (4) Fergana: the Ibrahim Tamghach Khan page puts the Western suzerainty over the rulers of Farghana in 1059/60, six years before Cliopatria's 1066, which is kept; (5) after 1211 the Kara-Khanid page has the Kashgar rebels surrender to Kuchlug in 1214, so the Tarim rump is no one's but the rebels' in 1212-1213 (see kara-khitans). Pages: seven distinct (budget 5) because of the fixes. Still missing: the extent of the rump beyond Kashgar and Khotan, and who held Aksu, Kucha and Khotan in 1212-1213.
